In mlx5 path: `xsk_buff_get_metadata` → `__xsk_buff_get_metadata` reads flags with READ_ONCE into `flags` local and validates. Then `xsk_tx_metadata_request(&meta, ...)` re-reads `meta->flags` directly (no READ_ONCE) and passes `meta->request.csum_start/csum_offset/launch_time` raw to the driver callback. That is a re-read of shared metadata — but does validation exist there? In `__xsk_buff_get_metadata`, validation is only on flags (unknown bits check and launch_time length check). csum_start/csum_offset are not validated at this layer — the driver callback does the validation.

Let me look at `mlx5e_xsk_request_checksum` in mlx5/core/en/xdp.c line 314, and xdp.c:508 and xdp.c:656 call sites of xsk_tx_metadata_request.

input.description: Read mlx5 xdp.c checksum/metadata call sites

content.thinking:
mlx5: csum_start/csum_offset from `meta` are re-read in `xsk_tx_metadata_request()` and passed to `mlx5e_xsk_request_checksum()`, which ignores them (HW/FW parsing, offsets ignored). So the second read flows into a function that ignores the value → benign. And there's no bounds validation of csum_start/csum_offset in the ZC driver path anyway (no validated-then-used split — the values are simply never used). Not a variant.

Note: flags re-read in xsk_tx_metadata_request is a second read, and flags→csum_read consistency isn't guaranteed; but since csum values are never validated/used in a memory-unsafe way, it's benign (also documented in the seed commit note).
